To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the expression of genes related with maternal behavior, such as the genes related with dopamine (DAT, DRD4), the opioid receptor (OPRM1), serotonin (5HRT2A) and GABA (GABAbRI), is higher in the MPOA in postpartum females that are exposed to pups than in virgin females that are not exposed to pups, and higher in virgin females that were exposed to pups than postpartum females who were not exposed to pups.
maternal behavior and the hormonal milieu associated with parturition are associated with changes in gene expression in brain areas associated with maternal behavior.

the microarray analyses of the MPOA and the MeA of postpartum females that are exposed to pups and engage in maternal behavior showed that genes associated with the dopaminergic, opioid, and serotonergic systems are upregulated in these brain regions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the neurobiology of mothering and the neurobiological changes that occur as a function of the hormonal, neurochemical, and behavioral events associated with pregnancy and mothering.
the identification of genes that are involved in the neuroendocrine control of maternal behavior.
the molecular mechanisms of maternal behavior, and the present study is an important first step in understanding the role of the genes in this process.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
maternal behavior is a complex behavior that involves many factors and many brain structures.

the microarrays were able not only to identify, on the transcriptional level, the candidate genes involved in the maternal behavior and the surrounding factors, but also to provide the first step in the process of identifying the genes that are involved in the neuroendocrine changes that are related to motherhood.
the pattern of expression in the MPOA is more related to maternal behavior than to the hormonal milieu associated with parturition.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the MPOA is a site of expression of genes that are associated with dopamine, opioids, and serotonin, and the MeA is a site for expression of glucocorticoid genes.

the MPOA and the MeA have different gene expression patterns, with the MPOA having a higher number of genes related to dopamine and the MeA having a higher percentage of genes related to glucocorticoids.
the genes that were up-regulated in both MPOA and MeA in response to pups and parity are those that regulate the stress response, the dopaminergic system and the opioid system.
The main takeaway from our work is that

microarray analysis of gene expression in the MPOA and MeA can be used to determine the pattern of expression for genes that are associated with the hormonal and neurobiological changes that occur with pregnancy and mothering.
the microarray technique is a powerful tool for the analysis of gene expression in the brain.
the microarray technique can be used to identify genes involved in the neurobiology of maternal behavior.
